title: Fixed-zero-input key collision on two-round AES-128, QBD 2025 full version

target.description: Initial AddRoundKey, one full round, then a final SubBytes/ShiftRows/AddRoundKey round; standard AES-128 key schedule and round keys starting from the master key.

setting.key_relation: The adversary constructs two distinct keys; no unknown related-key encryption oracle is assumed.
assumptions: The common input is the prescribed all-zero 128-bit block.
The objective is E_k1(0)=E_k2(0) for distinct chosen keys, not recovery of an unknown key.

time.note: Expected collision work in the source inbound/outbound cost model; no conversion to full-AES encryption units is made.

data.note: No separate external-oracle data budget is reported; a fixed input is not data complexity one.

memory.note: Qualitative source statement without a byte or block count; not interpreted as zero.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing budget is reported.

success.description: The source prices expected work for one collision, not a numerical probability of finding at least one at that fixed budget. Inbound DDT characteristic probability is distinct from the GD-generated starting-point distribution; outbound probability is conditional on an admissible inbound point. Published witness pairs and implementation timings are not a trial-denominated experimental success rate.

review.scope: Exact-edition targeted success audit of defining constructions and parameter-specific cost/probability passages; not a new full-paper/forward audit. Weak-key/structure fractions, local false matches, raw Grover marked fractions and whole-attack success stay distinct.

components.description: PDF17–18 Section4.2: source inbound characteristic model, not the probability that the GD procedure generates a starting point or the whole attack succeeds.
PDF17–18 Section4.2: source outbound characteristic conditioned on a conforming starting point. Sufficient degrees of freedom or expected one collision does not quantify finite-budget success.

evidence.locator: Table 1 p.6, Section 4.2 pp.17-18; Table 6 p.35, first 2-round AES-128 pair; author verifier lines 338-380 for round convention.
evidence.interpretation: The fixed-zero construction and theoretical work estimate belong to this paper's own Section 4.2, not the earlier claims discussed in Section 4.1. A concrete pair is independently checked locally.

evidence.locator: Complete exact primaryPDF1–58, all sections, displayed formulas/tables/algorithms, proofs and references.
evidence.interpretation: Full contribution inventory read; bounded forward checking and finite component validation are separately receipted. Full attack reproduction not attempted.

evidence.locator: PDF17–18 Section4.2, defining characteristic,degree-of-freedom and complexity paragraphs.
evidence.interpretation: The source prices expected work for one collision, not a numerical probability of finding at least one at that fixed budget. Inbound DDT characteristic probability is distinct from the GD-generated starting-point distribution; outbound probability is conditional on an admissible inbound point. Published witness pairs and implementation timings are not a trial-denominated experimental success rate.

limitations: The local verifier checks one published collision, not the search algorithm, expected work or practical timing.
This two-round result does not settle the full-round fixed-zero-input AES question.
